facts.quote: Sentinel lymph node from a patient with breast cancer, from the public CAMELYON16 dataset.
facts.basis: CAMELYON16 is a public set of H&E sentinel lymph node sections from breast cancer patients (Radboud UMC and UMC Utrecht; camelyon16.grand-challenge.org; Ehteshami Bejnordi et al., JAMA 2017).

facts.quote: No clinical history is published with the slide.
facts.basis: The CAMELYON16 release has whole-slide images and lesion annotations, no per-slide clinical record (manifest source fields).

facts.quote: You are looking at a 3.7 mm × 3.7 mm region inside the H&E section, not the whole section.
facts.basis: 15,360 px × 0.243094 µm/px = 3.73 mm; manifest.source.regionLevel0 places the window at (36,864, 66,560) of a 97,792 × 214,016 px scan; tissue fraction of the window 0.953.

facts.quote: Most of this region is lymphoid tissue, which looks dense and dark at low power because lymphocytes have dark nuclei and little cytoplasm.
facts.basis: Standard histology. Area check: the largest deposit's outline covers 3.36 of 13.94 mm² (24 %) of the region.

facts.quote: This is the background: sheets of small lymphocytes with round, dark nuclei and very little cytoplasm.
facts.basis: Location (3181.6, 3181.6) µm at 20×, 1.44 mm from the deposit outline; level-2 tile tiles/2/6_6.jpg viewed by the spec author: dense small lymphocytes, a paler sinus-like area at its right edge.

facts.quote: The largest deposit is the large pale area of cohesive tumour cells in the centre of this region.
facts.basis: The CAMELYON16 outline 'Annotation 3' (class Tumor) spans 2.61 × 2.22 mm around the region centre; tiles/2/3_2.jpg shows sheets of large cells with abundant cytoplasm.

facts.quote: Upper border: round clear spaces between bands of dark lymphoid tissue
facts.basis: Point (9300, 1000) px, 522 µm outside the outline; tiles/3/2_0.jpg: clusters of round clear spaces (likely fat) between lymphoid bands.

facts.quote: Lower right corner: dense, dark-staining lymphoid tissue
facts.basis: Point (13088, 13088) px, 1.44 mm outside the outline; tiles/2/6_6.jpg.

facts.quote: Centre: sheets of large, pale cells with abundant pink cytoplasm
facts.basis: Point (7168, 5120) px, inside the outline, 459 µm from its edge, in no Exclusion; tiles/2/3_2.jpg.

facts.quote: Lower edge: round and slit-like clear spaces within lymphoid tissue
facts.basis: Point (6400, 13900) px, 784 µm outside the outline; tiles/3/1_3.jpg.

facts.quote: Tumour cells that reach a lymph node through its afferent lymphatics usually lodge first in which compartment?
facts.basis: Standard: lymph-borne metastases arrive in the subcapsular (marginal) sinus first (option B marked correct).

facts.quote: Afferent lymphatics open into the subcapsular sinus under the capsule, so lymph-borne tumour cells usually lodge there first and can then spread into the rest of the node.
facts.basis: Standard lymph node anatomy and the usual pattern of nodal metastasis.

facts.quote: This region is a window inside the node, so the capsule may not be visible here.
facts.basis: Hedged: not verified whether the capsule lies inside the 3.7 mm window.

facts.quote: By the CAMELYON16 reference outline, the largest deposit measures about 2.7 mm in greatest dimension, so it is a macrometastasis.
facts.basis: Maximum Feret diameter of the convex hull of 'Annotation 3' = 10,948 px × 0.243094 µm/px = 2.66 mm (minimum Feret 1.94 mm); the manifest's region was chosen around the slide's largest tumour outline.

facts.quote: In the AJCC system for breast cancer, a nodal metastasis larger than 2.0 mm is a macrometastasis; one larger than 0.2 mm but not larger than 2.0 mm is a micrometastasis; clusters not larger than 0.2 mm are isolated tumour cells (AJCC also uses a 200-cell count for the two smaller categories).
facts.basis: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual, 8th edition, breast: pN definitions (macrometastasis > 2.0 mm; micrometastasis > 0.2 mm and/or > 200 cells, none > 2.0 mm; ITC ≤ 0.2 mm or < 200 cells in one cross-section).

facts.quote: This item asks for the size category of the deposit, not the nodal stage, which also depends on how many nodes are involved.
facts.basis: AJCC pN categories combine deposit size with the number of positive nodes.

facts.quote: Cells lying together in cohesive sheets or clusters
facts.basis: Marked correct: cohesion favours carcinoma over lymphocytes.

facts.quote: Nuclei larger than those of the lymphocytes
facts.basis: Marked correct.

facts.quote: More abundant cytoplasm
facts.basis: Marked correct (with the histiocyte caveat in F21).

facts.quote: This describes the lymphocytes.
facts.basis: Option D (small, round, dark nuclei with very little cytoplasm) marked incorrect.

facts.quote: Sinus histiocytes also have abundant cytoplasm, so cohesion and nuclear features matter; when the distinction is uncertain, immunohistochemistry for cytokeratin is commonly used to confirm epithelial tumour cells in a lymph node.
facts.basis: Standard practice (cytokeratin IHC, e.g. AE1/AE3, for nodal carcinoma).

facts.quote: The smaller outlined areas inside it are marked Exclusion: non-tumour tissue inside a tumour outline, by the dataset's convention.
facts.basis: CAMELYON16 ASAP annotation group 'Exclusion'; the six Exclusion polygons of this region all lie inside 'Annotation 3' (computed).

facts.quote: three small separate tumour foci
facts.basis: Three further Tumor polygons in the region ('Annotation 4–6'): greatest dimensions 0.05, 0.07 and 0.15 mm, outside the main outline (70–950 µm away).

facts.quote: The carcinoma cells are larger than the lymphocytes, with more cytoplasm and larger nuclei, and they lie together in cohesive sheets.
facts.basis: Location (2738.2, 1369.1) µm at 20×, 33 µm inside the outline's right edge; tiles/2/5_2.jpg: large tumour cells left, lymphocytes right.

facts.quote: That is tumour too: one of three small separate foci in the CAMELYON16 outline.
facts.basis: As F23.
